classification.difficultyReason: Use the triangle angle sum and a three-part ratio to justify that one angle is a right angle.

content.prompt: The angles in a triangle are in the ratio $1:2:3$. Show that this must be a right-angled triangle.

answer.short: The angles are $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, so it is a right-angled triangle.
answer.worked:
The angles in a triangle add to $180^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}
\text{Total parts} &= 1+2+3=6\\
1\text{ part} &= 180^\circ\div6=30^\circ\\
\text{First angle} &= 30^\circ\\
\text{Second angle} &= 2\times30^\circ=60^\circ\\
\text{Third angle} &= 3\times30^\circ=90^\circ
\end{align*}$$

One angle is $90^\circ$, so the triangle is right-angled.
